claims.text: W-Ta-Mo-Nb-V is described as a refractory high-entropy alloy composed of Group IV-V transition metals.
LMD or DMD can fabricate a W-Ta-Mo-Nb-V refractory high-entropy alloy.
The feedstock should be gas-atomized W, Ta, Mo, Nb, and V powder with oxygen below 80 ppm.
A powder particle-size range of 45-125 μm is suitable for deposition.
Suitable deposition parameters include 500-600 W laser power, 8-12 mm/s scanning speed, and 0.08-0.1 mm layer thickness.
Deposition should be performed in argon containing less than 80 ppm oxygen.
The deposited alloy should be HIP-treated at 1200-1300 °C for 2-4 hours at 100 MPa.
HIP should be followed by annealing at 1000-1100 °C for 1-2 hours.
The optimized final microstructure is a single-phase BCC solid solution.
The optimized final microstructure has fine equiaxed grains smaller than 10 μm.
The optimized final microstructure retains a high dislocation density.
Rapid solidification during LMD or DMD suppresses constitutional segregation and produces fine equiaxed grains.
Low-oxygen powder minimizes brittle oxide inclusions and thereby mitigates interstitial-related brittleness.
HIP eliminates porosity and residual stress-induced defects.
HIP dissolves brittle intermetallic phases.
Annealing refines and stabilizes the alloy as a single-phase BCC microstructure.
Solid-solution strengthening and grain-boundary strengthening enhance ductility and high-temperature strength in the proposed state.
The alloy will exceed 800 MPa compressive strength and 5% compressive strain at room temperature.
The alloy will exceed 500 MPa compressive strength and 10% compressive strain at 1000 °C.
Conventionally cast W-Ta-Mo-Nb-V alloys have coarse, segregated microstructures and high brittleness caused by interstitial impurities and brittle intermetallic phases.

contradictions.description: The alloy is labeled as a Group IV-V transition-metal family, but the listed elements include Mo and W, which are Group VI elements; no Group IV element is listed.

The hypothesis predicts that low oxygen and HIP/annealing improve properties, so observing poorer properties for high-oxygen material made without post-processing would support rather than falsify the proposed causal direction.
